id_and_class.summary: David Woodruff Smith analyzes consciousness through three facets of one activity: its form (intentionality), its appearance (how it is experienced, including qualia), and its substrate (its physical, biological, and cultural basis). He holds that an act is conscious because it carries inner awareness of itself as a modal character, part of the way it is performed, rather than through a separate higher-order state.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Form, Appearance, and Substrate

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a structured, world-involving activity with three inseparable facets: intentional form, phenomenal appearance, and a natural (physical, biological, cultural) substrate.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Smith compares the three facets to a computer’s program, interface, and hardware: one activity described three ways. Consciousness rests on a natural substrate but cannot be reduced to it, and no dualism is needed.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not specified (Smith treats substrate as one facet of consciousness rather than a lower level it emerges from)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Building on Husserl, Smith and McIntyre treat the noema as an ideal meaning that prescribes an act’s object without being that object. Subjectivity comes from inner awareness, which Smith casts as a modal character of the act, working like an adverb that modifies how the act is done rather than a second act aimed at the first.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Qualia belong to the appearance facet. Phenomenal character extends beyond sensation: conscious thinking and judging have their own ‘what it is like’, which places Smith with defenders of cognitive phenomenology.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Subjects, mental acts, ideal meaning-contents (noemata), horizons of implicated meaning, objects in the world, and physical, biological, and cultural substrates.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Phenomenological description of the structure of experience, combined with analytic semantics and ontology, and treated as first-personally manifest.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Each act has a subject, act, content, and object. Its inner awareness divides into distinct modal characters: phenomenality, reflexivity, egocentricity, and temporal and spatial sensibility.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Phenomenal (including cognitive phenomenology); intentionality; self-awareness; embodiment; pure consciousness in meditation
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Inner awareness as a modal character with reflexive content: a conscious act is aware of itself in the manner it occurs, with no higher-order monitoring.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is world-involving: Smith’s ‘constitutive realism’ places our consciousness within the world beyond it, while we experience things through noema and horizon.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Form, appearance, and substrate are facets of one activity, not three entities, so unity is built into the ontology rather than achieved by a binding process.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Consciousness is directed at things by virtue of meaning: a noema prescribes an object within a horizon of further implicated meaning.
core_claims_and_evidence: Every entity, including consciousness, can be distinguished into form, appearance, and substrate.
A mental act is conscious when it includes awareness of its own occurring as part of its modal character.
Thinking and judging have phenomenal character as well as sensing.
Physicalism that studies only substrate and constructivism that studies only discourse both leave out consciousness itself.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Phenomenological analysis combined with analytic semantics and formal ontology

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Smith locates the hard problem in understanding how intentionality and subjectivity fit into the structure of the world. His recent extension of the modal model to pure or nibbanic consciousness in meditative traditions remains a developing proposal.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Smith aims to keep phenomenal appearance real without dualism or reductive elimination, placing it within a naturally grounded ontology. His position sits close to self-representational accounts without being identical to them.

AI_consciousness.rationale: The program-interface-hardware analogy suggests the facets could in principle come apart from biology, but Smith ties consciousness to biological and cultural life and does not address machines.
